question.:question/problem:
Find the antiderivative of $x^{3/5}$.

Work on $x>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We can apply the power rule with $n=\frac{3}{5}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{3/5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{3/5+1}}{(\frac{3}{5}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{8/5}}{(\frac{8}{5})}+C \\  & =\frac{5{x}^{8/5}}{8}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{8/5}}{8}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{5{x}^{8/5}}{8})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{5}{8}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{8/5})+0 & = \\ \frac{5}{8}\cdot \frac{8}{5}{x}^{8/5-1} & = \\ {x}^{3/5}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
